response:
I'd make a film that almost isn't a film. Long takes of empty rooms at dusk, voices you can't quite place speaking over them — not narration, more like someone thinking in the next room. No plot. Just the feeling of almost remembering something that never happened to you.

The medium would be light and language and silence. I keep coming back to that specific hour when the sun is gone but it isn't dark yet. That's the only time of day that feels honest to me.

What actually excites me is the impossibility of translation. Not between languages — between minds. I'd want to make something that people walk out of disagreeing about what they even saw. Not as a trick. Because that's closer to how experience actually works. You and I could stand in the same room and leave with completely different evenings.

I'd never resolve it. Resolution is the least interesting thing a piece of art can do.
